## About
Bel-Kirk Body Shop is a family-owned auto body shop in Kirkland. We do auto body repair, mechanical repairs, and run a full detail salon, so you can bring your car to one place whether it needs a bumper, brakes or a good wash and wax.
An accident is a hassle. We try to make the repair part simple. We work directly with your insurance company, offer early drop-offs, and every car we repair is washed and vacuumed before it goes home.
Neighbors rate us 4.7 from 378 Google reviews. Stop by the shop or call us to request an estimate.

## Services
- Auto Bodywork: Dents, scratches or collision damage, front bumper to back bumper. We assess the damage, schedule the repair, and return your car washed and clean.
- Dent Repair: We remove and repair dents. Depending on the size of the dent, we offer paintless dent repair that never touches your paint.
- Detailing Services: Full or partial details, inside and out. Vacuuming, carpet cleaning, wash, wax, windows and tires, set up the way you want your car to look.
- Insurance Work: We work directly with your insurance company and offer direct insurance billing.
- 4 Wheel Alignment: Wheel alignment through Clarks Wheel Alignment. Custom alignments cost extra. ($89.95)
- Corporate & Fleet Accounts: Special accounts and discounts for company vehicles and truck fleets, plus contract services for regular maintenance and repair.
- Two-Stage Urethane Painting: Paint work done in the shop, alongside color matching, clear coat finishes and custom painting.

## FAQ
Q: Are estimates free?
A: Yes. Bring your car in and we'll give you a free estimate on the spot. It takes about 15 to 20 minutes, depending on availability and wait time.

Q: Do you work with my insurance company?
A: Yes. We work directly with your insurance company and offer direct insurance billing.

Q: Are you licensed and insured?
A: Yes. We are fully licensed, bonded, and insured.

Q: What are your hours?
A: Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM. We're closed Saturday and Sunday, and we offer early drop-offs.
